correctness.rationale: For the minimal permutation DFA, the group of input actions is transitive and the reverse subset states are its orbit on the final set. Transitivity distinguishes all different reverse subset states and makes exactly two of them incident to each original state. The incidence-signature injection follows from forward DFA minimality. Hence 2N=tm and N<=binom(t,2), so t>=m+1 and N>=binom(m+1,2). Equality forces a bijection to edges of a complete graph and a 2-homogeneous group action; conversely any such edge action with a vertex-star final set is minimal forward, and its reversal has precisely two accepting stars. The proof covers every integer m>=2 and both directions of the equality classification. Explicit independent DFA minimization passed m=2..12; finite checks are not the all-m proof.

originality.rationale: The 2022 paper derives constraints on attainable numbers of accepting states under reversal, not the least total forward state count. The 2026 paper constructs for each m,alpha a witness using binom(m+alpha-1,alpha) forward states, hence gives the alpha=2 upper bound. Its complete proof establishes existence and minimizes each constructed DFA, but does not universally minimize the witness cardinality or classify all state-minimizers. The new incidence lower bound and rigidity characterization answer those separate optimization questions. The accessible own deduplication claims and the published research index searches revealed no same lower bound or 2-homogeneous equality classification; this does not establish global uniqueness.
residual_risks: Other unindexed or terminology-divergent papers may have studied optimal witness size rather than only attainable final-state counts.

value.rationale: The minimal number of forward states needed to realize a prescribed pair of reversal accepting-state counts is a natural optimization refinement of a solved existence spectrum. The sharp quadratic lower bound explains why the known binomial-size witness cannot be compressed for reverse accepting count two. More importantly, equality forces a complete edge-incidence system and 2-homogeneous transition group, classifying all optimal automata, a structural theorem not implied by one explicit witness. The result is an all-m theorem, not a small tabulation or an arbitrary parameter slice; larger reverse counts remain open in this analysis.
